import pandas as pd

homes = pd.read_csv("demo_homes.csv")

avg_size = homes.groupby("neighborhood")["sqft"].mean().round(0)
counts = homes.groupby("neighborhood")["sqft"].count()

print("Average home size (sqft) by neighborhood:")
print(avg_size)
print()
print("Homes per neighborhood:")
print(counts)

answer_key.mechanism: The sqft column is complete, each neighborhood average rests on a group of thirty homes, and the group sizes are printed beside the averages so the reader can judge them. The claim -- average size by neighborhood -- is exactly what was computed.
caveats: An average hides spread: two neighborhoods with the same mean sqft can have very different mixes of homes.
Size is not value -- nothing here says which neighborhood is more expensive per square foot.
